_do_not_hand_edit: Every number here is computed from the CURVES table in the generator. Verify with `python3 research/modalities/emc_ipd_survival.py --check`.

method.citation: Guyot P, Ades AE, Ouwens MJNM, Welton NJ. Enhanced secondary analysis of survival data: reconstructing the data from published Kaplan-Meier survival curves. BMC Med Res Methodol 2012;12:9.

what_this_is: Patient-level survival data reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. A reconstruction is a re-expression of a published figure -- never new patients, never new follow-up, and it inherits every selection effect of the series it came from.

quality_floor.rationale: Without a numbers-at-risk table the per-interval censored count is unidentifiable. A curve below the floor is REFUSED, not pooled with a caveat.

curve_schema.endpoint: one of: os | dss | pfs | lrfs | dmfs
curve_schema.population: free text -- the arm or stratum this curve describes
curve_schema.digitized: list of [time, survival_probability], time non-decreasing, S non-increasing in [0,1]
curve_schema.risk_table: list of [time, n_at_risk], time non-decreasing, n_at_risk non-increasing
curve_schema.total_events: integer if the paper prints it, else null
curve_schema.digitized_by: who read the figure, and with what tool -- provenance for a hand step

status: NO CURVES DIGITIZED. The instrument is built and its known-answer control passes; no published EMC figure has been read into CURVES yet. Digitizing a figure requires the figure, and inventing a coordinate would fabricate a clinical datum. This field is the honest state, not a placeholder to be filled in with plausible numbers.
